messages:
dalia: quick heads-up — ran a small profiler sweep on the host parsing path. for short requests (~<32 tokens) we're spending ~12-18% CPU in tokenization + proto parsing before the model sees anything. p95 latency for tiny requests bumped ~20ms.
mike: ugh. sounds like host-side fixed overhead visible when model latency is tiny. can you paste the flamegraph snippet? :mag:
sara: saw similar in last week's canary. looked like lots of time in grpc::Unmarshal and our tokenizer allocate path.
pranav: is this the same KV-cache-hot-shard spike from friday? or separate? wondering if kvcache eviction churn is causing extra parsing (retries/etc).
dalia: separate — kvcache looks fine for these traffic patterns. this is pure parse/tokenize + writev overhead on streaming responses. i captured a small perf dump:

```
# perf top (host parse)
- crypto/hpack_decode               18.2%
- grpc::Unmarshal                   14.5%
- host_tokenizer::tokenize          12.4%
- writev_coalesce                   8.1%
- http2_frame_handler               7.9%
```

mike: crypto/hpack is interesting — header decode cost for each small request. if clients aren't reusing keep-alive connections, setup costs matter.
sara: also the tokenizer path has a hot alloc path we can fastpath. i sketched a patch: reuse a thread-local tokenizer buffer and avoid per-request vector growth.
pranav: for streaming chunking: we do small chunks (~256b) which end up emitting many writev entries. if we coalesce to ~2KB on host for very low latency flows we should reduce syscall overhead without hurting latency.
dalia: ran a micro-experiment on canary with two changes: 1) tl-token-buffer reuse + bump reserve to 2K, 2) coalesce streaming chunks writev threshold at 1.5KB, 3) short-circuit header parse when connection id matches cached decode. results (median over 10k small requests):

- baseline median: 68ms
- patch median: 52ms
- baseline p95: 112ms
- patch p95: 88ms

cpu consumption on host parsing thread dropped ~15%.

mike: nice. did you check behavior under burst? batching heuristics could interact — more coalescing might delay first-byte for some patterns.
sara: yes — synthetic burst tests with poisson arrivals showed <1ms additional first-byte in 99th for steady bursts, but big wins in syscall reduction.
pranav: any risk to KV cache or kernel selection heuristics? re: kernel selection, if the host parse latency drops, overall scheduling might favor smaller batch sizes — we need to ensure our batcher doesn't shrink too aggressively.
dalia: good call. i ran the batching sim with reduced host overhead and it nudged the autoscaler to target slightly smaller continuous batches (more latency-sensitive). we should add a floor to batch size for throughput tiers.

mike: what about gRPC framing settings? can we tune window sizes or SETTINGS to reduce hpack runs?
dalia: i added a quick cache keyed by (conn_id, last_headers_hash) to avoid full HPACK decode for repeated trivial headers. it's small and TTLed. that removed ~50% of crypto/hpack time in the perf run.
sara: will open a PR with the tokenizer TL buffer + header cache + writev-coalesce. include benchmarks & perf scripts.
pranav: please add a short failure mode: if coalesce buffer goes beyond 5ms delay threshold flush early. also add metrics: host_parse_cpu, writev_syscalls, header_cache_hits.

deploy-bot: rolling canary started for sha=ca7b9e3 -> 10% traffic.

dalia: action items:
- sara: PR with tests + microbench (tokenizer + writev) — blockers?
- prAnav: add batcher floor experiment + metric alerts
- mike: run end-to-end regression on KV-heavy workloads
- ops: monitor host_parse_cpu & header_cache_hits during canary

sara: on it. PR ready in a couple hours, will link perf artifacts.
mike: i'll prep the KV-runbook scenario.
pranav: i'll add experimental flag to batcher and flag the autoscaler config.
dalia: thanks all — this looks like a low-risk host-side perf win with measurable latency and cost upside. will sync tomorrow if canary looks good. :thumbsup:
